findings.source_passage: I declare to you, that for the time I lived as in a musky meadow; I forgot all about our horrible oath; in that inexpressible sperm, I washed my hands and my heart of it
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'As I sat there at my ease'
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'I lived as in a musky meadow' is one of the most iconic lines in this chapter and the entire novel — a culturally famous, critically discussed moment of sensory dissolution. The draft excises it entirely, jumping from the spring-violets simile directly to 'I forgot our horrible oath,' destroying the rhetorical climax of the sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim: 'I declare to you, that for the time I lived as in a musky meadow' before the 'I forgot our horrible oath' clause.

findings.source_passage: Such an abounding, affectionate, friendly, loving feeling did this avocation beget; that at last I was continually squeezing their hands, and looking up into their eyes sentimentally
findings.why_it_matters: The word 'loving' is dropped from the famous string 'abounding, affectionate, friendly, loving' — a signature rhetorical list. The anaphoric rhythm and the inclusion of 'loving' carry major interpretive weight for homoerotic / communal-love readings that the critical tradition depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'loving' to the list: 'abounding, affectionate, friendly, loving feeling.'

findings.source_passage: Would that I could keep squeezing that sperm for ever! For now, since by many prolonged, repeated experiences, I have perceived that in all cases man must eventually lower
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Would that I could keep squeezing'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft drops 'that sperm' from 'keep squeezing that sperm for ever' and omits 'since by many prolonged, repeated experiences' — the latter being the ruminative, autobiographical framing that gives the philosophical turn its voice-weight. Without it the paragraph reads as bare assertion rather than earned reflection.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'that sperm' and the clause 'since by many prolonged, repeated experiences' to preserve Ishmael's ruminative voice.

findings.source_passage: In thoughts of the visions of the night, I saw long rows of angels in paradise, each with his hands in a jar of spermaceti.
findings.source_locator: end of paragraph beginning 'Would that I could keep squeezing'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft renders this as 'In visions of the night' — dropping 'In thoughts of,' which gives the sentence its peculiar doubled, distanced quality (thoughts of visions). The signature phrasing is subtly but consequentially altered.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the exact phrasing: 'In thoughts of the visions of the night.'

findings.source_passage: It tasted something as I should conceive a royal cutlet from the thigh of Louis le Gros might have tasted, supposing him to have been killed the first day after the venison season, and that particular venison season contemporary with an unusually fine vintage of the vineyards of Champagne.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Plum-pudding is the term bestowed'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft cuts the extended absurdist elaboration about Louis le Gros being killed 'the first day after the venison season' and the Champagne vintage — the entire comic tail of the simile that makes the passage distinctive and funny. What remains is the bare simile, stripped of its voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full extended simile through '...unusually fine vintage of the vineyards of Champagne' to preserve the absurdist comic register.

findings.source_passage: Now, while discoursing of sperm, it behooves to speak of other things akin to it, in the business of preparing the sperm whale for the try-works.
findings.why_it_matters: This transitional sentence is a register-establishing, self-consciously discursive marker of Ishmael's narrator voice ('it behooves to speak'). The draft replaces the entire transition with the abrupt 'Of kindred matters:' — erasing the essayistic, mock-formal tone that defines this chapter's second half.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the transitional paragraph or at minimum the 'it behooves' framing to preserve the discursive narrator voice.

summary: The draft commits one unambiguous high-severity signature erasure (loss of 'I lived as in a musky meadow'), a second high-severity loss (dropping 'loving' from the climactic list), and four medium-severity voice-flattenings including the Louis le Gros comic tail, the 'In thoughts of the visions' phrasing, and the discursive transitional voice — together requiring regeneration.
